papers.title: On tensor products of CSS Codes
papers.read_provenance: Prior sidecar full-text fetch and inspected theorem passages; reused, not fetched again in this extension.
assumptions: Binary CSS pair C2 contained in C1-perp, full-rank check matrices, paired logical quotient bases.
For every basis coordinate in both orientations, a family in its specified single detector coset, cardinality at least N>0, overlap at most K>0.
Lemma 2.7 requires at least one factor complex balanced; post-Theorem-2.8 discussion allows separate bases for the orientations.
papers.conclusion: Tensor-product distance at least ceil((N/K)*d(D)); Corollary 2.11 yields the single-complex bound ceil(N/K).
papers.mapping: Predecessor of the existing overlap counting; product construction not needed for the single-code consequence.
papers.missing_hypotheses: Does not itself state a mixed-detector-class family conditioned on an exact logical residue.
papers.counterexample_risk: Incomplete coordinate coverage cannot be promoted to a global lower bound.
papers.useful_next_lemma: Uniform pairing on a coordinate fiber, then apply the existing weighted theorem.

papers.title: The disjointness of stabilizer codes and limitations on fault-tolerant logical gates
papers.read_provenance: Prior sidecar full-text fetch; reused inspected Lemma 2 and Lemma 4 statements.
assumptions: Nontrivial noncommuting logical classes G and G-prime; fixed qudit partition; c-disjoint set of distinct representatives.
Scrubbing: arbitrary region H, positive integer c no greater than m^(n-k).
papers.conclusion: Delta_c(G) <= d(G-prime); some g in G has Delta_c(G)*|supp(g) intersect H| <= |H|.
papers.mapping: Common-anticommutation support counting matches the local pairing-one theorem.
papers.missing_hypotheses: The original statement fixes one detector class and uses sets rather than multiplicities.
papers.counterexample_risk: Pairing one with a reference alone is not uniform unless boundary orthogonality is established.
papers.useful_next_lemma: Transfer reference pairing across boundary differences within a full coordinate fiber.

papers.title: Finding the disjointness of stabilizer codes is NP-complete
papers.read_provenance: Prior sidecar full-text fetch; reused inspected Theorem 5 and LP definitions.
assumptions: Any stabilizer code; one fixed nontrivial logical Pauli class.
Nonnegative variables for every representative; each physical-qubit load at most one.
papers.conclusion: LP optimum equals supremum over positive integer c of c-disjointness, attained at finite c.
papers.mapping: Natural-weight finite certificates; same quotient-image pools become a fixed class after stabilizer extension.
papers.missing_hypotheses: The theorem does not supply a successful packing or the mixed-class sector coverage adapter.
papers.counterexample_risk: A dual optimum restricted to stored columns is not a global obstruction; floating-point weights are not exact certificates.
papers.useful_next_lemma: Conditional finite weighted certificate with exact strict 6*cap < totalWeight.

papers.title: Stabilizer Codes and Quantum Error Correction
papers.version: arXiv v1; identified by fetched abstract metadata
results: Section 3.2 standard stabilizer-space and normalizer construction (not a numbered expurgation theorem)
assumptions: Commuting independent stabilizer generators with compatible phases, excluding minus identity.
For the proposed extension, fifteen pure-X cycles independent modulo old X boundaries.
papers.conclusion: A stabilizer of rank n-k defines a 2^k-dimensional code; nontrivial logical Pauli operators are normalizer elements modulo stabilizers and phases.
papers.mapping: Adjoin fifteen X checks without changing 566 physical positions; ranks 289/274, k=3.
derived_inferences: S contained in S-prime implies N(S-prime) minus S-prime contained in N(S) minus S, modulo phases: the old global lower bound six is preserved.
Residual Z logical space equals the annihilator of the added detector span.
H_X/U pairs perfectly with Ann(U); four quotient classes pair one with any fixed nonzero residual class.
papers.missing_hypotheses: Independence, cycle membership, and good-family bound-seven statements still require certificates.
papers.counterexample_risk: A larger lower bound for an extended code does not transfer backward; an original upper witness can become a stabilizer.
papers.useful_next_lemma: Residual-logical identification and conditional span extension, without changing the physical norm.

papers.title: Improved constructions of nested code pairs
papers.version: Latest abstract metadata v3 (2017-07-18); full text read at unversioned HTML endpoint
results: Relative generalized Hamming weight definition before Theorem 2
assumptions: Strict nested linear codes C2 contained in C1 contained in F_q^n.
papers.conclusion: CSS sector distances are M1(C1,C2) and M1(C2-perp,C1-perp); M1 minimizes physical weight in C1 minus C2.
papers.mapping: Residual Z objective is M1(Z_K,B_Z), with quotient dimension three and the original physical metric.
papers.missing_hypotheses: The paper-specific polynomial-code bounds are not shown applicable to these literal matrices.
papers.counterexample_risk: Higher relative weights concern support unions, not merely chosen basis-vector weights.
papers.useful_next_lemma: Identify residual logicals with the nested-code difference Z_K minus B_Z.

papers.title: Coding Theoretic Construction of Quantum Ramp Secret Sharing
assumptions: Any strict nested pair C2 contained in C1 contained in F_q^n; physical-coordinate subset J; induced quotient projection maps.
papers.conclusion: The recoverable subsystem includes dim(Ptilde_J(kernel Ptilde_complement)) qudits; full recovery is characterized by full quotient rank on J and zero on its complement.
papers.mapping: Precedent for explicit quotient-map and kernel bookkeeping.
papers.missing_hypotheses: This is not an overlap certificate or a minimum-distance bound for the target.
papers.counterexample_risk: An abstract logical-coordinate projection is not a Hamming isometry on physical vectors.
papers.useful_next_lemma: Well-defined coordinate fibers and boundary-difference equivalence.

papers.title: CSS code surgery as a universal construction
assumptions: Sandwiched pushout with separated shared logical-operator subcomplex as in Definition 6.6.
X lower bound in Lemma 6.7 requires k_T = k_C+k_D-1.
Error-corrected procedure additionally requires the merged Z distance not below the initial direct-sum distance, explicitly defined in Definition 6.8.
papers.conclusion: Conditional X-distance preservation and conditional error-corrected surgery; Appendix F shows a merge lowering Z weight.
papers.mapping: Supports postponing grafting unless dimension and physical-weight hypotheses can be certified.
papers.missing_hypotheses: No automatic final Z lower bound and no source-578 bound.
papers.counterexample_risk: A correct chain/pushout construction can lower distance.
papers.useful_next_lemma: Nontrivial logical lifting with explicit physical-weight control in the vulnerable sector.

papers.title: Engineering CSS surgery: compiling any CNOT in any code
papers.version: Latest abstract metadata v3 (2025-06-27); full text read at unversioned HTML endpoint
results: Section 4.2.2 (scope and auxiliary-distance discussion, not a new distance theorem)
assumptions: Z-preserving maps are chain maps; X-preserving maps are cochain maps.
Fault-tolerance discussion requires an auxiliary code with sufficient distance.
papers.conclusion: Preserving code maps induce logical maps, but their definitions do not impose a physical Hamming-weight bound.
papers.mapping: Separates logical-map correctness from the norm control needed for distance transport.
papers.missing_hypotheses: Unconditional source-578 lower bounds and a suitable target-to-source weight inequality remain absent.
papers.counterexample_risk: Introducing a logical qubit can reduce distance; a chain map is not a metric guarantee.
papers.useful_next_lemma: A nontrivial source lift with the required explicit weight bound.
